programme.title: Небо на Земле. На каком языке Бог говорит с людьми?
programme.desc: Не секрет, что читать Библию трудно, особенно тем, кто только начинает, поэтому многие спрашивают: может ли простой человек понять Бога и нужно ли тратить силы на то, что непонятно? Ответ находится во Втором Послании Фессалоникийцам, 2:10. Бог объясняет нам Себя и Свои планы через образы и предметы, которые нам понятны, так план спасения во всех деталях объяснен в образах и деталях земного Святилища. programme.desc: Современная тенденция «сглаживать углы» снижает опасность греха, и прихоти главенствуют в жизни. Человек становится зависим от прихотей и видит Бога обязанным исполнять его желания. В таком положении человек становится противником Бога. Бог ждет верности и преданности человека через покаяние. Бог хочет сделать человека свободным от похотей. Ведущий: Мария Мараханова, Гость: Михаил Долженко, священнослужитель

programme.title: Взаправду. Футбол по правилам и без
programme.desc: Для того, чтобы поступать правильно, не обязательно все всегда знать. Иногда достаточно прислушиваться к хорошим советам. Но если иногда результаты своеволия не очень страшны, то порой непослушание приводит к очень плохим последствиям. Надя Мартыканова рассказывает библейскую историю о том, как Адам и Ева не послушались Бога и отведали плод с дерева познания добра и зла. В результате стали несчастны не только они, но и все их дети, потому вместе с непослушание в мир проникло зло. Ведущий: Надежда Мартыканова, Марк Латухин

programme.title: Ну дела! Правила общения
programme.desc: В любом возрасте хочется найти друзей. Что делать, чтобы нравиться людям и с тобой хотели общаться? Существуют ли секреты дружбы и секреты общения? Каких друзей нужно выбирать и как правильно общаться? Всем известно, что осуждать характер и перебивать человека не стоит. Наоборот, нужно говорить очень приятные слова. Нужно знать, как правильно принимать подарки. В программе можно узнать об основных правилах общения и о том, с кем можно поговорить в любое время. Ведущий: Сережа Сироткин, Маша Грачева

programme.title: Библия. Синодальный и церковно-славянский переводы
programme.desc: Многосерийный фильм «Библия». Библия на Руси появилась позже, чем в других странах, но все же уже существовала на местном языке задолго до появления Синодального перевода. Это был церковнославянский перевод Священного Писания. Какова роль Синодального и церковнославянского переводов Библии? История Российского Библейского общества. Ведущий: Анатолий Руденко, исполнительный директор РБО, Гость: И. Лобанов, ведущий научный сотрудник Института перевода Библии им. М. П.Кулакова, А. Синицын, магистр в области религии, священнослужитель, А. Десницкий, доктор филологических наук, профессор РАН, Н. Гузов

programme.title: Возрождение. Дух Святой меняет нас
programme.desc: Никто не может стать настолько порочным или пасть так низко, чтобы сила Святого Духа не могла в нем произвести свою очистительную работу. programme.desc: Современная тенденция «сглаживать углы» снижает опасность греха, и прихоти главенствуют в жизни. Человек становится зависим от прихотей и видит Бога обязанным исполнять его желания. programme.title: Взаправду. Футбол по правилам и без
programme.desc: Для того, чтобы поступать правильно, не обязательно все всегда знать. Иногда достаточно прислушиваться к хорошим советам. Но если иногда результаты своеволия не очень страшны, то порой непослушание приводит к очень плохим последствиям. Надя Мартыканова рассказывает библейскую историю о том, как Адам и Ева не послушались Бога и отведали плод с дерева познания добра и зла. В результате стали несчастны не только они, но и все их дети, потому вместе с непослушание в мир проникло зло. Ведущий: Надежда Мартыканова, Марк Латухин

programme.title: Ну дела! Правила общения
programme.desc: В любом возрасте хочется найти друзей. Что делать, чтобы нравиться людям и с тобой хотели общаться? Существуют ли секреты дружбы и секреты общения? Каких друзей нужно выбирать и как правильно общаться? Всем известно, что осуждать характер и перебивать человека не стоит. Наоборот, нужно говорить очень приятные слова. Нужно знать, как правильно принимать подарки. В программе можно узнать об основных правилах общения и о том, с кем можно поговорить в любое время. Ведущий: Сережа Сироткин, Маша Грачева

programme.title: Wild Holland - The Living Delta
programme.desc: The film celebrates the diverse natural heritage of the Dutch delta region while sketching the cultural context that has played such a vital part in shaping it. Using cutting edge cinematic techniques ranging from eagle’s eye aerial views to unprecedented underwater scenes, 'Wild Holland - The Living Delta' presents a portrait of this unique wetland area of Europe as never seen before, capturing it in an important moment of change - a time when new life is flooding back into the delta.

programme.title: mareTV: Hong Kong - Metropolis in the sea
programme.desc: Hong Kong translated means "fragrant harbour". The days of the spicy smoking ceremonies have passed, but MareTV has discovered many delightful contrasts between the metropolis and Mother Nature. In for-mer times, the rare eagle wood tree grew here. Its wood put the spice into the Taoist smoking ceremonies. The fragrant harbour: what sounds so charming is today a huge metropolis in the sea. No other tiny piece of land is more densely populated. Star Ferries have been commuting between the Kowloon Peninsula and central Hong Kong for the past 125 years. The British colonial masters are long gone, but on the ancient ferries, virtually nothing has changed. Most of the ships are still clad in British Racing Green and the crew still wears the old, decorative uniforms.

programme.title: World's Most Dangerous Railway Lines
programme.desc: The Tanzania-Zambia-Railway (Tazara) is one of Africa's most ambitious infrastructure projects. It connects the inland with the coast of East Africa and meant independence from the surrounding apartheid-ruled countries of East Africa. The film accompanies the Tazara on its 52-hour journey through Tanzania and Zambia and uses spectacular aerial shots to show not only the architectural monuments but also the unknown sides of the previously hidden landscapes of Tanzania and Zambia.

programme.title: World's Most Dangerous Railway Lines
programme.desc: In northern Argentina, the world-famous Tren a las Nubes - the cloud train - crosses dizzying viaducts and deep valleys. At an altitude of over 4000 meters, what was once the highest railway runs past cactus forests and into the driest desert in the world. A technical feat in the Andes and a breathtaking ride through spectacular scenery.In northern Argentina, the world-famous Tren a las Nubes - the cloud train - crosses dizzying viaducts and deep valleys. At an altitude of over 4000 meters, what was once the highest railway runs past cactus forests and into the driest desert in the world. A technical feat in the Andes and a breathtaking ride through spectacular scenery.

programme.title: Germany's Wild Reservoirs
programme.desc: One of the smallest dams in the Bergisches Land is the Panzertalsperre, with an area of just four-and-a-half football pitches. On the other hand, the Dhünntalsperre is the largest with the area of 660 football pitches. They all transform a stretch of flowing water into still and stagnant water. As a result, completely diverse ecosystems have developed there: where the dipper once dived for insect larvae, cormorants and gray herons now fish and swans and coots cavort. In recent summers, even greater challenges have emerged: the effects of climate change - from extreme drought to destructive floods. On a smaller scale, a rather industrious dam master is operating flood protection: The Beaver. However, the water masses of the Wupper tore away half of his majestic timber castle - and the four young beaver kids were not seen again afterwards. Have they survived the flood? Not everyone can cope with the constant change in the dams, but they still remain an important wonder of engineering for many: for us humans as well as for a number of animals. By combining water management, ecological requirements and tourism a worthwhile goal is possible: Because for the Bergisches Land, its dams are among the most valuable and popular infrastructures that the region has to offer.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.desc: Olympic National Park is an American national park located in the State of Washington, on the Olympic Peninsula. The park has four regions: the Pacific coastline, alpine areas, the west side temperate rainforest and the forests of the drier east side. Within the park there are three distinct ecosystems which are subalpine forest and wildflower meadow, temperate forest, and the rugged Pacific coast. President Theodore Roosevelt originally designated Mount Olympus National Monument on 2 March 1909. The monument was redesignated as a national park by Congress and President Franklin Roosevelt on June 29, 1938. In 1976, Olympic National Park was designated by UNESCO as an International Biosphere Reserve, and in 1981 as a World Heritage Site. In 1988, Congress designated 95 percent of the park as the Olympic Wilderness.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.desc: Yosemite National Park is a place of superlatives: with towering cliffs and giant sequoias, home to coyotes, black bears and the most elusive of all: the bobcat. Watch this documentary with ist spectacular shots, aerial views and time-lapse shots and learn some new facts about the biodiversity in one of North Americas most spectacular National Parks.

programme.title: Discover Poland
programme.desc: The world‘s best helicopter camera system - the Cineflex Camera - was used for this documentary and delivered fantastic images in HD quality, revealing the surprisingly diverse landscapes and fascinating towns of Poland from a bird‘s eye view of Poland‘s medieval towns, the modern silhouette of Warsaw, the untouched nature of the border regions between east and west, the coasts to the north and the mountain ranges of the south

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Roads are more than just gray strips of asphalt that allow us to travel and trade. For centuries they have been lifelines of mankind, full of stories and history - and in certain countries and areas they also hold great dangers, much human suffering and death. Documentary filmmaker Oliver G. Becker ventured onto the dangerous roads of Afghanistan's Hindu Kush Mountains, the infamous Moloto Road in South Africa, along the vertiginous slopes of the Bolivian Andes and other "roads of death" in India, Georgia and the Ivory Coast

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Some risks on these car routes have natural causes: Extreme weather, avalanches and landslides. In some areas, the locals even believe that evil spirits kill travelers. But many of the dangers are man-made: robbers or terrorists lie in wait for travelers, and tough labor pressures, social hardship and greedy mass-transit businesses also cause tragic driving accidents around the world. In the 20th century alone, 35 million people died on roads worldwide - plus 1.5 billion injured!

programme.title: One Year in Norway's Lofoten
programme.desc: Winter means more than just the beginning of the year for the people of Lofoten: For more than a thousand years, Lofoten has been a hub for cod fishing, with seasons lasting from February to April as huge shoals migrate from the Barents Sea to these waters. During these hectic months, more than 65,000 tons of fish are brought to shore, securing the income for the whole of Lofoten for years to come. Around a quarter of the fish caught ends up on lines to dry upon racks. From a young age, the children from the fishing villages get to earn some pocket money by cutting cod tongues and selling the produce as a delicacy appreciated by the locals.

programme.title: One Year in Norway's Lofoten
programme.desc: Almost unnoticeably, spring turns into summer. The days become longer and longer, with a never-setting sun. People who have spent their winter and spring working hard can finally enjoy their own nature, even though the temperature is only slightly warmer. Lofoten is sparsely populated, just 24,000 people live here. Unstad is one of its smallest communities with only 15 inhabitants, but despite that, it has become a hotspot for arctic surf and is host to the northern-most surf center in the world. Surfers from all over the globe come to surf in the arctic water.

programme.title: Wild Faces of the Andes
programme.desc: The Andes are the biggest mountain range in the world. Peaks of up to 7000 metres in height, do not only offer an imposing view, but also influence the climate by being the drainage and meteorological divide.

programme.title: mareTV: Newfoundland - Canada's Eastern Point
programme.desc: In Newfoundland, at the easternmost tip of North America, the landscape is pristine, dramatic, and very sparsely populated. In summer, icebergs occasionally drift along the steep cliffs. When the "Titanic" collided with an iceberg and sank just 300 miles off the coast of Newfoundland in 1912, the last radio messages were picked up in a small wooden hut on the Avalon Peninsula. Today, most Newfoundlanders live on Avalon. There are particularly many seabirds here. In Witless Bay, the newborn puffins are ready for their first descent into the Atlantic. But some stray onto the coastal road, attracted by the lights of the hotels and restaurants. In doing so, they run the risk of being run over. A team of volunteers saves the lives of countless young birds: The Puffin & Petrel Patrol goes out at night dressed in high-visibility vests to collect the puffins. Biologist Sabrina Wilhelm then brings them back to Green Island, home to the largest puffin colony in North America. Here, the birds catch up on what they should have done long ago: the first dive of their lives.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: The Carretera de la muerte - the road to death- is one of the most dangerous roads in the world. Year after year many people die here. We accompany trucker Omar and his co-driver Jaime on their trip across the Andes, encountering cyclists, mountain bikers and coca-farmers on the way.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: The racing cyclists of Burundi have a dangerous job. But it’s a vital one for Burundi’s economy. Bicycles are the main means of transportation in one of the smallest countries in Africa. Bananas, the staple food in Burundi, are transported from the markets to a banana beer brewing factory. We accompany Tharcien, a bike courier, on his exhausting cross country trip on the Burundi Highway.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: The Sichuan Tibet Highway is the road of longing for many. It leads through fascinating landscapes and remote areas up to the Himalayan Mountains. We accompany truck driver Ren Taiping on his trip to the Tibetan capital city of Lhasa, encountering pilgrims, mountain bikers and nomads on this dangerous journey.

programme.title: Gronland - In the Glare of Ice
programme.desc: Greenland is the largest island in the world and the landmass closest to the North Pole. 80% of the country is covered by a layer of ice up to 3000 meters thick. Most of the inhabitants of the country are spread over the breathtaking landscape of the ice-free west coast. The country is mostly inhabited by Inuit, who have been feeding on what nature has provided them for thousands of years. But the original life is in a state of change. The modernisation of society and man-made global warming threaten the Arctic natural paradise that is so incredibly important for our planet. Through the eyes of locals we get to know the authentic Greenland.

programme.title: mareTV: Madeira - Portugal's sea of blossoms in the Atlantic Ocean
programme.desc: Flower magic in Madeira: The Flower Festival Festa da Flor is the most important event of the year for the people of the Atlantic island. With it they celebrate spring, which is climatically practically all year round here, their island and themselves. The coast formed by lava, centuries-old laurel forests and green steep slopes make Madeira unique. Those who start right at the front of the big parade of the flower festival in the capital Funchal, will have made it. For Isabel Borges this dream has come true. She opens this year's flower parade along the harbour promenade with her festive group. This accolade does not only mean fame and prestige, but also a lot of pressure. Are the self-designed dresses splendid enough? Will the 150 flower children learn the dance steps in time? Will the flowers on the float hold out in the heat? For Isabel, it is now a matter of nerves.

programme.title: Dream Islands of Europe: Lanzarote and Fuerteventura
programme.desc: The film presents the two Canary Islands Lanzarote and Fuerteventura. Lanzarote has a rich culture in addition to a volcanic landscape: the film accompanies a ceramic artist, an instrument maker, shows architecture by César Manrique and a camel breeder. On Fuerteventura, in addition to livestock farming and the operation of traditional grain mills, nature conservation plays a major role: islanders are committed to preserving the sand dunes, and there is a turtle hatchery. On Lanzarote, countless volcanic eruptions have formed a bizarre lunar landscape. It is a great challenge for the inhabitants to extract the cultivation of food from the karstic, dry soil. And yet they even manage to produce wine. Protected by thousands of small depressions that act as water reservoirs, they grow vines on porous volcanic rock.

programme.title: mareTV: La Palma: The Greenest of the Canaries
programme.desc: Thundering waterfalls, ancient forests and an impressive volcanic landscape with black beaches: La Palma is a dream island for nature lovers. It is by far the island of the Canary Islands with the most green, almost half of it is covered with forest. But once a year the green island is dominated by the color white. On Rosenmontag (Rose Monday), the inhabitants have for decades been targeting those ancestors who returned from abroad wealthy and ostentatiously demonstrated their wealth with powdered faces. The carnivalistic approach culminates every year in a white chaos, with tons of talcum, flour or paint trickling down the uniformly white dressed islanders. On the Roque de los Muchachos, La Palma's highest mountain at 2,400 meters, stands one of the largest reflecting telescopes in the world. Astrophysicists love the island because it is the perfect place to look into space. Researchers and star lovers look spellbound to Beteigeuze. The giant star is probably in front of a supernova and could become a second moon in the firmament.

programme.title: Fuerteventura: The golden beauty of the Canaries
programme.desc: Fuerteventura, the second largest of the Canary Islands, is located just 120 kilometres off the coast of West Africa. The climate is extremely dry and the struggle for water has always been a major setback. Then, around a century ago, returning US emigrants brought what were then modern wind turbine water pumps from the Aermotor Windmill Company with them to Fuerte-ventura. Today, the environmentally friendly and so-called “Chicago’s”, experience a renaissance. Unfortu-nately, original spare parts in good condition are diffi-cult to come by. When Leocadio Araya Sanchez began planting countless cacti on a barren hillside a few years ago, people thought he was mad. His idea was to make a healthy juice drink from the prickly pears – with great success. But getting the fruit to release its pre-cious superfood juice is no simple task. On an almost daily basis, Marcos Tapia is magnetically attracted to one of the paradisiacal beaches of the island. The 44-year-old is Spanish champion and vice world champion in para-body board surfing. When he was 28. Marcos was involved in a serious motorbike accident and has been paraplegic ever since.

programme.title: 45 Minuten Thüringen
programme.desc: In einer Koproduktion der lokalen TV-Sender in Thüringen bringt Moderator Mike Langer Politik ganz nah an die Menschen. In jeder Folge trifft er auf Politikakteure oder -beobachter aus dem Freistaat Thüringen und beleuchtet nicht nur die politischen Themen der Region, sondern auch die Persönlichkeiten hinter den Entscheidungen.Was bewegt die Menschen, die über Thüringens Zukunft entscheiden? Welche Geschichten und Erfahrungen prägen ihre Arbeit? ?45 Minuten Thüringen? liefert unterhaltsame und tiefgründige Einblicke in den politischen Alltag und zeigt dabei mitunter auch eine andere Seite der Politik. Freuen Sie sich auf offene Gespräche, aktuelle Analysen und persönliche Anekdoten ? für alle, die Thüringen und seine Macher besser verstehen wollen.

programme.desc: Abdullah and his friends build a tower to lookout for his lost father. Tha Abdullah agus a charaidean a’ togail tùr-fàire gus sùil a chumail a-mach airson athar.

programme.title: A’ Chùil
programme.desc: Tha Choirstaidh air ais le prògram eile bhon stiùidio aice, A’ Chùil. Sa phrògram seo tha i ag ath-chuairteachadh seann chofaidh airson fosailean a dhèanamh a tha a’ coimhead dha-rìribh ro-eachdraidheil. Choirstaidh is back in her arts studio and makes fossils by recycling used coffee grounds.

programme.title: Dùbhlain DIY (Instructions Not Included)
programme.desc: Derek Pluto Murray hosts as three couples tackle sport and fitness-themed challenges.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Musician and learner Andrew Findlater joins Joy in the studio and Calum Maclean takes an earthly walk, provoking thoughts of space and the galaxies around us.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Lios Mhàiri/Mairi’s Hebridean Garden
programme.desc: Mairi visits growers at a thriving community garden in Cranhill, Glasgow.

programme.title: Hebridean Baker - Nordic Islands
programme.desc: Coinneach MacLeod explores the food traditions of Gotland in Sweden. Tha Coinneach MacLeòid a’ faighinn blasad de chultar a’ bhidhe ann an Gotland san t-Suain.

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Mary Ann and Lucy hunt the 'good for you' plants and those that definitely aren’t.

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara/Mermaid Tales
programme.desc: Kate travels around Barra and meets people from the community who tell her about the history of the place.

programme.title: Faodail
programme.desc: Tha Tasglann Fhilm Faodail a’ tarraing aire gu filmichean dhùthchasach Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 80an, a bha caillte ach a-nis glèidhte don ghinealach ri teachd. Tha bhana Cinema Sgìre Leantainneach a’ siubhal nan eilean, a’ taisbeanadh fhilmichean sna sgìrean ionadail, le cothrom am faicinn air-loidhne air feadh an t-saoghail. Cuirear aithris bheairteach ùr riutha, a’ buntainn ris a’ Ghàidhealtachd, airson luchd-amhairc an là an-diugh. The Faodail Film Archive celebrates lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s to the 1980s in the Outer Hebrides, preserving the archive for future generations. The Cinema Sgìre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands, showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online, and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gàidhealtachd for contemporary audiences. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Machair
programme.desc: Drama Gàidhlig stèidhichte ann an Leòdhas. Gaelic soap set on the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc: Là àbhaisteach eile ann a Fraochy Bay... gus am bheil rionnag laidir, deannte a' nochdadh a Ameirceidh. Tha Arnold Logan am beachd gum bi a h-uile duine mar e fhein ma cheannaicheas iad an stuth miorbhuileach a tha eisin a reic. Fuirich thusa ge tha, cha toir duine a char a cailleachan a bhaile seo, ge bith de cho laidir is a tha iad. American fitness freak Arnold Logan is invited to Fraochy Bay to sell his miracle muscle-gain products. Surely his promise of 'instant results for none of the work' is too good to be true?

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Prògram spioradail le laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean à Coats ann am Pàislig, air a lìbhrigeadh le Iain MacFhionghain. Am measg na seinneadairean bidh Ruairidh Gray, Hamish Scott, agus Rona NicLeòid le Donnchadh MacLeòid. Cuideachd, an còisir Binneas fo stiùir John Joe MacNèill. Bidh Angela NicAoidh a’ meòrachadh air cuspair creideimh le leughadh agus smuain, dàn is seallaidhean spioradail à Tiriodh ann an companachd Dòmhnall Eachann Meek agus bidh Chloe Steele a’ toirt dhuinn seirm adhraidh air a’ phìob à Manachainn nan Lios. Iain MacKinnon presents a mix of hymns, psalms and readings from Coats in Paisley. Amongst the singers performing are Ruairidh Gray, Hamish Scott and Rona MacLeod with Duncan MacLeod. Also appearing is the choir Binneas, conducted by John Joe MacNeil. Angela MacKay selects reading and thought, plus spiritual poetry and landscapes from Tiree in the company of Donald E Meek. Chloe Steele performs a tune of worship on the pipes from Beauly Priory. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Los Mosqueteros: El regreso a casa
programme.desc: Phortos regresa a las peligrosas calles de su juventud cuando es injustamente acusado de asesinato. Es decisión de los otros mosqueteros rescatarlo o no.

programme.title: Los Mosqueteros: Los exiliados
programme.desc: Aramis y D'Artagnan se frustran en su tarea de llevar a una joven y su bebé de un pueblo a palacio, cuando hombres armados secuestran al bebé. Deben averiguar quién es ella y por qué alguien llegaría tan lejos para secuestrar a su hijo.

programme.title: Los Mosqueteros: Una mujer rebelde
programme.desc: Los mosqueteros ayudan a salvar a una mujer condenada a muerte por brujería mientras que un misterioso envío papal de Roma hace todo lo que puede por detenerlos.

programme.title: Los Mosqueteros: El reto
programme.desc: El rey llama a una contienda entre los mosqueteros y los Guardias rojo para probar que ejército es mejor, lo que le da a D'Artagnan la posibilidad de probarse a sí mismo.

programme.title: Los Mosqueteros: Caballero toma reina
programme.desc: Los mosqueteros sitian un convento mientras protegen a la reina después de un ataque contra su vida por parte de un asesino, experto tirador.

programme.title: Los Mosqueteros: Los mosqueteros no mueren fácilmente
programme.desc: Una inesperada desavenencia amenaza con volar por los aires la relación entre los mosqueteros. ¿Podrán reparar el daño o Milady tendrá éxito en su destructiva revancha final?

programme.title: Los Mosqueteros: Mantén a tus amigos cerca
programme.desc: Los mosqueteros vuelven y deben rescatar a un general francés de una impenetrable prisión española.

programme.title: Los Mosqueteros: Un hombre ordinario
programme.desc: D'Atagnan debe proteger al rey Luis cuando un conocido criminal secuestra a ambos.

programme.title: Los Mosqueteros: El buen traidor
programme.desc: Los mosqueteros ayudan a rescatar a la hija de un enemigo a cambio de una fórmula mortal, pero su misión se complica cuando capturan a Phortos.

programme.title: Los Mosqueteros: Emilia
programme.desc: Los mosqueteros investigan a una mujer que dice tener visiones de Dios que le indican liderar sus miles de seguidores a una guerra con España.

programme.title: Los Mosqueteros: El regreso
programme.desc: Cuando secuestran a Athos y lo llevan a Pinon, él y los mosqueteros deben luchar con un noble para proteger a las personas abandonadas por Athos.

programme.title: Los Mosqueteros: A través de un vidrio oscuro
programme.sub-title: A través de un vidrio oscuro
programme.desc: Un astrónomo organiza una fiesta real para ver un eclipse pero los eventos toman un giro dramático y los mosqueteros son llevados al límite.

programme.title: Los Mosqueteros: Un matrimonio de inconvenientes
programme.desc: El primo del rey cae en una emboscada bajo la protección de los mosqueteros y otras figuras importantes de la corte parecen estar en peligro.

programme.title: Los Mosqueteros: El padre pródigo
programme.desc: Porthos descubre la verdad sobre su familia y cuestiona su lealtad. Los mosqueteros sospechan de la nueva familia de Phortos.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: A poster collection tops the bill in this episode from West Sussex. In Horsham, Charlie Ross marvels at historic posters collected by local man William Albery. Examples include an appeal for a stolen fat sheep, a concert to raise money for the victims of the Titanic and instructions on how to avoid catching Spanish flu. Each poster demonstrates the bold typography and social history that Albery loved so much. Hoping to post the biggest profit at auction is the red team, friends Kully and Arti, who reckon that the blues are going to lose. Their opponents are mum and daughter Judith and Tilly who are in it to win it. Among the stalls of Ardingly antiques fair, Kully spots colourful signs painted on scaffold boards, including one about kite flying – until expert Jonathan Pratt decides it may crash at auction. Inside, Judith spies a silver bookmark in the shape of a trowel. She’s thinking constructively – but expert Kate Bliss isn’t impressed by its lack of age. In Buckinghamshire, auctioneer Hugo Lemon works hard for the teams, but what can JP rustle up for his bonus buy – with only one pound to spend?

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is at Altrincham Recycling Centre in Greater Manchester with an eagle eye, hoping to swoop in on quality items before they are lost forever. A mysterious wooden post leaves lighting designer Duncan scratching his head, and Jacqui tries to get a dated rocking chair back in full swing. Will she manage to send all three items off to new homes?

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It's Children’s Week. In the Pattern Challenge, the sewers tackle a children’s tutu. In the Transformation Challenge, sustainability is key as the sewers repurpose fleece into stuffed animal toys with adorable results. Finally, mini models are welcomed into the sewing room for the Made-to-Measure Challenge. The sewers are tasked with creating an outfit for their very own superhero creations. Who will handle it like child’s play, and who will be sent to the naughty step?

programme.title: BBC News

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jessie Cave, Ayesha Hazarika, Simon Hickson and AJ Pritchard take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Edge
programme.desc: Gabby Logan takes charge of the quiz where contestants need brainpower and ball skills to win big. Who will be the high roller and who will push themselves over The Edge?

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Comedian and presenter Susan Calman, internet star Max Fosh and DJ Noreen Khan are back as the week moves on to its second stop. Vernon Kay keeps the quiz on track, while Traitors star Paul Gorton is back as an unreliable tour guide, turning the spotlight on Enniskillen and its surprising stories. With scores beginning to take shape, attention shifts towards who could become the week's overall champion.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: The lives of the park’s rock hyrax babies hang in the balance as their mum is taken to the vets for an urgent medical investigation. The keepers have spotted worrying lumps on the mum, Dozy, which might be affecting how her youngsters feed from her. With Dozy at the vets, the babies are alone, so it’s a race against time to do the investigation and get mum back to her babies before they get too hungry. Elsewhere, there are some arrivals in the park who have been missing since the mid-nineteenth century – red squirrels. Their numbers have dwindled as they face competition from the non-native grey squirrels that are destroying the natural parkland. The keepers are embarking on a red squirrel breeding programme to help save these beautiful animals from extinction in the UK, but they need to create an enclosure that encourages the squirrels to mate. Meanwhile, Kate helps keep the cheetah in peak physical condition with some high-intensity training, Ben creates a mud bath for the European wolves, and out on safari Jean Johansson learns how to recognise individual zebras and tests the eyesight of an ostrich.

programme.title: Serengeti
programme.desc: All our animal families make the most of the good times when a new oasis brings untold riches. But they face devastation when a towering inferno takes over. Will anyone survive?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: A set of musical drinking glasses, a pianists finger stretcher and Harry Lauder's piano give this edition from Dumfries a musical flavour. But Michael Aspel and the experts also find rare local silver, a valuable doll and a collection of drawings by Beatrix Potter worth a small fortune.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from the Watts Gallery in Surrey, a treasure trove of British art and sculpture. The experts Thomas Plant and David Harper are on hand to find a selection of objects to take to auction. Thomas values an art deco flapper girl, while a trio of pocket watches impresses David. Paul also visits the heathland known as the Devil's Punchbowl to uncover gruesome tales of highway robbery.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, former winners Jimi Famurewa, Harriet Kemsley, Colin Murray and Sara Pascoe take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall House of Champions winner being crowned on Friday. Will they opt for the House of Games golden cowboy hat, or instead go for the must-have golden wheelie luggage?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway journey reaches the naval port of Brest, home to France’s oceanographic fleet. Aboard the pride of the fleet, the 107-metre-long Pourquoi Pas, Michael hears how marine biologists deploy research submersibles 6,000 metres below the surface to study life in the deep sea. In the kitchen of a traditional boulangerie, Michael learns how to make a Breton favourite, a sweet, buttery cake called kouign-amann. The taste for Breton culture leads him to Guingamp, where he attempts to keep up with a Breton dance troupe rehearsing for the regional dance championships. On the windswept north coast, with some of the highest tides in the world, Michael visits Brittany’s largest nature reserve, which attracts over 100 bird species.

programme.title: Nigellissima
programme.desc: Nigella shares her culinary talent as she presents delicious Italian-inspired food. In this episode, Nigella reveals a secret passion for one of the tastes of Italy with her dark and deviant liquorice pudding, before introducing us to the joys of fregola - the Sardinian sun-dried and toasted couscous - in a light, tomato-hued recipe of couscous with clams. Nigella's dinner party guests are served a simple yet sumptuous meal of butterflied leg of lamb and baby aubergines with oregano and roasted red onion. Dessert is an irresistible meringue gelato cake with sharp raspberries and a dark chocolate sauce.

programme.title: Race Against the Tide
programme.desc: Six teams return to St Andrews Beach for a deeply personal challenge: sculpting what home means to them in just six hours, before the tide sweeps in. From Welsh valleys and family legacies to artistic studios and symbols of rebirth, creativity meets chaos as collapses and comebacks keep the pressure high. Judges Sadie and Jamie expect emotional depth and technical brilliance but don’t anticipate the surprise twist of an ending - so who will rise and who will crumble under the weight of the ever-looming waves?

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: When a mayday comes in from a yacht breaking up on a sandbank off the Norfolk coast, both the Great Yarmouth and Gorleston RNLI crew and two of Caister’s independent lifeboats race to the rescue. In Pembrokeshire, the St Davids crew are alerted to two paddleboarders in distress, but their location is eight miles away - and it will take at least half an hour to reach them. Just off the coast of Scarborough, a fisherman has slipped on rocks and has a suspected broken ankle; in fading light and a rising tide, the crew face a tricky extraction. And across the Irish Sea, in Skerries, there are reports of two swimmers in difficulty near Shenick Island.

programme.title: Emergency 24/7
programme.desc: Two trauma calls reveal that the greatest dangers are not always the most obvious, testing the expertise, judgement and resilience of the emergency team at Southmead Hospital. They battle to save Paul, whose leg has been severed after being hit by a train but who is in more immediate danger from an overdose that could cause severe liver damage. And they question the story of a man with a deep wound who denies being stabbed.

programme.desc: Mom Kelly says Ellie, 16, is on a path of self-destruction, & she fears for her daughter's life. Ellie has an eating disorder, is suicidal, cuts herself & has overdosed on drugs while lashing out in anger on a daily basis. Dr. Phil helps set a new path.

programme.desc: Christi & Nels say daughter, Nicole, 27, is an alcoholic drinking 1L of vodka a day, hospitalized 15 times for alcohol poisoning, & nearly died on 5 of those occasions. Nicole admits she's an "extreme alcoholic". Can Dr. Phil help this family in turmoil?

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Amanda, 25, says she was molested over 795 times by her father, Earl Nix, a secret when revealed to family was rejected despite Nix being convicted of first-degree criminal sexual conduct. The family comes face-to-face in an emotional attempt for truth.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Dr. Phil continues his mission to end the silence on domestic violence. More than 25 percent of battered women remain in a relationship with their abuser. Sonya fears that she is one of those women who stay. Hear her story.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.sub-title: Texas Police Chief Leading Secret Triple Life Pt.2

programme.desc: Carol & Tab's 20-year-old son, Alex, was killed by a hit-and-run driver. They believe that Alex's death was no accident claiming Rob, 24, of being responsible. Rob, joined by his family, say he's falsely accused & part of an "unrelenting witch hunt".

programme.title: Wir in Bayern - Das Schönste aus 2025
programme.desc: Wir in Bayern - Das Schönste aus 2025 - Zu Gast sind die Brüder und Reisefilmer Julian und Thomas Wittmann. Florian Lerche macht Saltimbocca von der Chiemsee-Renke auf buntem Bohnensalat und Conny Ganß stellt alkoholfreie Weine vor. Außerdem sendet "Wir in Bayern" "Grüße aus ..." Mähring und besucht den Hofladen Gotzenberg. In den Sommerferien blickt "Wir in Bayern" zurück auf die schönsten Momente aus dem Jahr 2025. Es gibt ein Wiedersehen mit inspirierenden Gästen und spannenden Geschichten. Und mit den leckeren Rezepten zum Kochen und Backen sowie hilfreichen Servicetipps wird das Wiederentdecken Freude bereiten.

programme.title: Frankenschau aktuell
programme.desc: Frankenschau aktuell - Heute: Kicken für Kinder: Sternstunden-Benefiz-Fußballturnier mit Promis in Bamberg Arbeiten am Limit: Würzburger Rettungskräfte im Hitzestress Segen fürs Leben: Haustiergottesdienst in Coburg Die Sendung berichtet werktags über das Geschehen in Ober-, Mittel- und Unterfranken. Täglich ist das Team in der Region unterwegs, um die wichtigsten Nachrichten aus Politik, Wirtschaft, Gesellschaft und Kultur aufzugreifen und verständlich aufzubereiten. Die Sendung bietet einen kompakten Überblick über aktuelle Entwicklungen und ordnet diese ein. Ergänzt wird das Programm durch Hintergrundberichte, Reportagen und Stimmen aus der Bevölkerung. Zudem rückt sie auch besondere regionale Initiativen ...

programme.title: Abendschau - Der Süden
programme.desc: Abendschau - Der Süden - Die Sendung berichtet von Montag bis Freitag über aktuelle Ereignisse, Menschen und Entwicklungen aus Bayern. Das Regionalmagazin greift Themen aus Politik, Wirtschaft, Kultur und Sport auf und zeigt, was die Menschen im Freistaat bewegt. Ob kommunale Herausforderungen, gesellschaftliche Debatten, besondere Freizeitangebote oder spannende Geschichten aus dem Alltag - die Sendung bietet einen vielfältigen Blick auf den Süden Bayerns. Mit Reportagen, Hintergrundberichten und Interviews informiert sie über regionale Themen und ihre Bedeutung vor Ort.

programme.title: Abendschau
programme.desc: Abendschau - Das bewegt Bayern heute - Seit 1954 informiert die "Abendschau" über Neuigkeiten und Wissenswertes aus dem Freistaat Bayern und zählt damit zu den ältesten Fernsehsendungen Deutschlands. Die regionalen Berichte werden häufig durch sorgfältig recherchiertes Hintergrundwissen ergänzt. Das Format umfasst zudem Beiträge zu Kultur und Musik. Gelegentlich führen die Moderatoren Gespräche mit Studiogästen zu aktuellen Themen. Darüber hinaus werden Entwicklungen aus Politik, Gesellschaft und Alltag regelmäßig eingeordnet und verständlich vermittelt.

programme.title: Lebenslinien
programme.desc: Die erstaunliche Frau Riedl und die Kinder in Indien - Anna Riedl kommt 1929 im Donau-Ries zur Welt. Die Mutter stirbt bei der Geburt Ihres dritten Kindes. Der Vater heiratet wieder, damit die Kinder eine Mutter haben. In der bäuerlichen Familie herrscht solcher Mangel, dass Annas Schwester zu Verwandten gegeben wird. Nach dem Krieg beginnt Anna in München eine Schwesternausbildung. Als sie diese abbrechen muss, öffnet sich eine Tür für ein völlig anderes Leben. Mangel und Not prägen Annas Kindheit im Donau-Ries. Mit Anfang 20 darf sie nach München, wo sie im Klinikum Dritter Orden Kranken- und Klosterschwester werden soll. Aufgrund einer infektiösen Knochenhautentzündung muss sie die Ausbildung jedoch abbrechen und darf nur als ...

programme.title: Space Night
programme.desc: Space Night - Heute: The Blue Planet Die Sendung nimmt die Zuschauerinnen und Zuschauer mit auf eine faszinierende Reise durch das Universum. Eindrucksvolle Aufnahmen und wissenschaftlich fundierte Animationen machen ferne Galaxien, Sterne und kosmische Phänomene erlebbar. Grundlage sind die Erkenntnisse modernster Observatorien und Teleskope, die mit hochentwickelter Technik immer tiefere Einblicke in das Weltall ermöglichen. Die Sendung verbindet anschaulich die jahrtausendealte Faszination für die Astronomie mit den neuesten Ergebnissen der Weltraumforschung und lädt dazu ein, die unendlichen Weiten des Kosmos zu entdecken.

programme.title: Dahoam is Dahoam
programme.desc: Schwerer Gang - Die Sendung erzählt Geschichten aus dem fiktiven oberbayerischen Dorf Lansing, wo Tradition, Gemeinschaft und dörflicher Alltag eng miteinander verwoben sind. Im Zentrum stehen die Familien und Bewohner, deren humorvolle, herzliche und manchmal konfliktreiche Erlebnisse den Charme der Serie ausmachen. Schauplätze wie der Brunnerwirt, der Dorfplatz oder die Werkstatt bilden den vertrauten Rahmen, in dem Beziehungen wachsen, alte Werte gepflegt und neue Herausforderungen gemeistert werden. So vermittelt die Serie ein Gefühl von Heimat.

programme.title: Sturm der Liebe
programme.desc: Sturm der Liebe - Adam findet für Werner einen neuen König für sein Schachspiel. Katja möchte Leo als Assistent einstellen. Kilian und Fanny pflanzen ihre Rose wieder in die freie Natur. Während Adam Olivia anvertraut, wie sehr er die nahen Momente mit Werner vermisst, gibt auch Werner vor Katja zu, dass ihn die Begegnung mit Adam nicht kaltgelassen hat. Als Adam mitbekommt, dass Werner den König seines antiken Schachspiels verloren hat, recherchiert er bis tief in die Nacht und findet tatsächlich einen neuen König. Er bittet Olivia, Werner den König zu geben und zu behaupten, sie hätte ihn gefunden. Olivia verspricht es und gibt Werner den König. Aber dann bekommt sie mit, wie Erik vor Werner schlecht ...

programme.title: Gym
programme.desc: Tele-Gym - Thema: Aerobic, Bewegung, Tanz (6/8) "Tele-Gym: Aerobic, Bewegung, Tanz": ein motivierendes Herz-Kreislauftraining, bei dem Ausstrahlung, Koordination, Fitness und Ausdauer verbessert werden mit viel Spaß bei jedem Training. Mit den Dance Workouts von "Tele-Gym: Aerobic, Bewegung, Tanz" wird der gesamte Körper von Kopf bis Fuß trainiert: Einfache Bewegungen aktivieren die Stoffwechselsysteme, der Kreislauf wird angeregt und Kalorien verbrannt. Langeweile kommt bei dem mitreißenden Dance-Training der Top-Presenterin Johanna Fellner nie auf: Schritt für Schritt baut sie die abwechslungsreichen Choreografien auf. Die jeweiligen Folgen haben unterschiedliche Schwierigkeitsstufen und ...

programme.title: Panoramabilder / Bergwetter
programme.desc: Panoramabilder / Bergwetter - Schon seit vielen Jahren eröffnen die allseits beliebten Panoramabilder aus Bayern, Österreich und Südtirol, begleitet von den lokalen und regionalen Wettermeldungen, allmorgendlich einen atemberaubenden Blick auf die Schönheit von Gebirgswelten, Landschaften und Städten im stetigen Wechsel der Jahreszeiten.

programme.title: Tele-Gym
programme.desc: Tele-Gym - Heute: Emotional Moves (6/8) Rückenschmerzen sind die Zivilisationskrankheit Nummer Eins. Die beste Therapie besteht in der aktiven Vorbeugung durch gezieltes Training! Um den Rücken komplett zu trainieren braucht der Übende allerdings von Zeit zu Zeit neue Herausforderungen. Johanna Fellner zeigt effektive Trainingseinheiten für einen starken und gesunden Rücken. Beugende, streckende und rotierende Bewegungen sowie statische Ganzkörperpositionen und Balanceübungen ergeben ein optimales Gesamtpaket. Der Zuschauer lernt die Positionen sicher auszuführen und die Atmung sinnvoll zu integrieren. Die gesamte Rumpfmuskulatur, insbesondere der Rücken, wird gekräftigt, stabilisiert und ...

programme.title: Elefant, Tiger & Co
programme.desc: Unter Strom - Die Zoo-Doku-Soap "Elefant, Tiger & Co" beleuchtet den Alltag hinter den Kulissen eines der renommiertesten Zoologischen Gärten Europas. Zebramädchen Klara ist auf der Afrikasavanne hinter den Stromzaun geraten und irrt nun in dem abgetrennten Bereich hin und her. Der Rückweg scheint ihr versperrt. Ihre Mutter Dolly hat die Lage erkannt und wird allmählich nervös, doch helfen kann sie ihrer Tochter nicht. Glücklicherweise kommt in dem Moment Jens Hirmer an der Savanne vorbei und erkennt die brenzlige Situation. Elefantenbulle Voi Nam wurde vor mehr als 16 Jahren in Leipzig geboren. Nach der Zeit in der Jungs-WG in Heidelberg ist er zurückgekehrt und inzwischen zu einem stattlichen Bullen ...

programme.title: Geisterkatzen - In den Bergen der Pumas
programme.desc: In den Bergen der Pumas - In Patagonien, weit im Süden von Chile und inmitten der schroffen Gebirgskette der Anden, verbirgt sich ein ganz besonderer Ort. programme.title: Corporate: Trademarq
programme.desc: Hampton DeVille schließt sich mit einem Straßenkünstler zusammen, der die Firmenzentrale beschädigt hat, um Anti-Konzern-Merchandise zu verkaufen und von den Gegnern zu profitieren.

programme.title: Corporate: Firmen-Klausur
programme.desc: Auf der Firmen-Klausur von Hampton DeVille bringen Business-Gurus Matt bei, wie man selbstsicherer wird. Jake findet Liebe bei einer Networking-Party.

programme.title: Corporate: Casual Friday
programme.desc: Matt und Jake haben Mühe, einen Kollegen zu überzeugen, am Casual Friday ein Hemd zu tragen, und Christian bemüht sich, mit einer Gruppe von Megakirchen einen Handel abzuschließen.

programme.title: Corporate: Das lange Meeting
programme.desc: John und Kate müssen die Leitung eines Meetings übernehmen, als Christian einen Anruf erhält. Sie schließen das Personal ohne ihre Handys im Konferenzraum ein, bis sie mit dem Brainstorming fertig sind.

programme.title: Corporate: Die Gesellschaft von morgen
programme.desc: Während die Mitarbeiter besessen von einer hochkarätigen TV-Serie sind, widersteht Jake ihren Versuchen, ihn dazu zu bringen, sie ebenfalls anzusehen. In Matts Leben passiert indessen auf unheimliche Weise das Gleiche wie in der Serie.

programme.title: Corporate: Wochenende
programme.desc: John drängt Jake und Matt, ihm zu helfen, eine Standuhr in sein Apartment zu bringen, und sabotiert damit ihre Wochenendpläne.

programme.title: Corporate: Tag der Erinnerung
programme.desc: Matt bewältigt sein Familientrauma, indem er sich in die Büro-Weihnachtsfeier stürzt, Christian hinterfragt sein Weltbild, und Jake zieht in Erwägung, die Firma zu verlassen.

programme.title: Corporate: Mattchiavelli und der Detektiv
programme.desc: Es kommt Unruhe auf, als die Mitarbeiter bei Hampton DeVille erfahren, dass kontrolliert wird, wie oft sie ihre Schreibtische verlassen.

programme.title: Takeshi's Castle Thailand
programme.desc: Hundert Kandidaten stehen bereit, um die Burg von Takeshi zu stürmen. Sie müssen das turbulente Tauziehen überstehen und beweisen, dass sie das Zeug dazu haben, die Leibgarde zu besiegen.

programme.title: Takeshi's Castle Thailand
programme.desc: Eine neue Gruppe Kandidaten will die Burg stürmen. Sie müssen die Trittsteine und das Torwandrennen überwinden, ohne im Dreck zu landen. Werden sie es bis zum finalen Angriff schaffen?

programme.title: Takeshi's Castle Thailand
programme.desc: Eine neue Gruppe Kandidaten stellt sich der fliegenden Klette und der Bienenwabe, um sich für den finalen Angriff auf die Burg zu qualifizieren. Wer schafft es, und wer bleibt im Schlamm stecken?

programme.title: Takeshi's Castle Thailand
programme.desc: Die Leibgarde steht bereit, als eine neue Gruppe Kandidaten versucht, die Burg zu stürmen. Zuvor müssen sie allerdings den Fliegenpilz, die Rollbahn und das Sumoringen überstehen. Wer schafft es zum finalen Angriff?

programme.title: Takeshi's Castle Thailand
programme.desc: Der General versammelt erneut hundert Kandidaten, die den Felsenkanal, den Schildkrötenweg und die Fallgrube überwinden müssen, bevor sie die Burg von Takeshi stürmen können. Hat einer von ihnen das Zeug dazu?

programme.title: Takeshi's Castle Thailand
programme.desc: Hundert Kandidaten müssen das Wasser (und die Piraten) des Schildkrötenwegs überwinden, bevor sie sich der Malzeit stellen, um die Burg stürmen zu können. Der General sieht zu. Wird einer es schaffen?

programme.title: Takeshi's Castle Thailand
programme.desc: Hundert neue Kämpfer wollen die Burg erstürmen und den General stolz machen. Doch wer kann das Bowlingspiel, die Rutschwand und die Hängebrücke überwinden?

programme.title: Takeshi's Castle Thailand
programme.desc: Es ist schmutzig, es ist verrückt, es ist Takeshi's Castle. Hundert neue Teilnehmer müssen sich dem Torwandrennen und der fliegenden Klette stellen, bevor sie die Fallgrube überwinden und die Burg angreifen können.

programme.title: Takeshi's Castle Thailand
programme.desc: Neue Kandidaten versuchen, die Burg zu stürmen. Doch schaffen sie es angesichts der Bowlingbahn und der wackeligen Hängebrücke? Vor dem Sieg müssen die Konkurrenz, die Aufgaben und die Leibgarde überwunden werden.

programme.title: Takeshi's Castle Thailand
programme.desc: Hundert mutige Kandidaten treten an, um Takeshis Burg zu stürmen. Zuerst müssen sie aber Wasser, Schlamm und viele andere unschöne Dinge überwinden. Nur die Stärksten können es schaffen.

programme.title: Most Ridiculous: Die verrücktesten Hunde
programme.desc: Most Ridiculous, die schrägste Clipshow von allen, ist zurück und widmet sich diesmal dem besten Freund des Menschen. Wir haben alles - von Halunken in Hundegestalt bis hin zu verwöhnten Vierbeinern.

programme.title: Most Ridiculous: Die verrücktesten Eltern
programme.desc: Most Ridiculous, die verrückteste Clipshow im Fernsehen, ist zurück. Diesmal stehen Eltern im Rampenlicht - von faulen Vätern bis hin zu tollpatschigen Müttern.

programme.title: Most Ridiculous: Die verrücktesten Modesünden
programme.desc: Most Ridiculous, die abgedrehteste Clipshow von allen, ist zurück. Diesmal geht es um Modesünden - von Chaos auf dem Laufsteg bis hin zu verunglückten Fotoshootings.

programme.title: Most Ridiculous: Die verrücktesten Talentshows
programme.desc: Most Ridiculous, die abgedrehteste Clipshow von allen, ist zurück. Diesmal geht es um Talentshows - mit der ganzen Palette von miserablen Theatereinlagen bis hin zu musikalischen Totalversagern.

programme.title: Most Ridiculous: Die verrücktesten Autofahrer

programme.title: BizTalk | AI-powered travel reshaping global tourism
programme.desc: China’s tourism market has continued to heat up this summer. Behind this boom, artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how people travel and is opening up new opportunities for the industry – from personalized itineraries to immersive experiences. In this episode of BizTalk, guests from the World Economic Forum, the World Travel & Tourism Council and Atout France explore how smart technologies can enhance visitor experiences, optimize destination management and unlock new growth opportunities. They also examine what China's emerging "AI tourism" focus could offer the global tourism industry.

programme.title: Meet China: When Chinese Dynamism Reshapes Landscapes — Boundless Challenges, Infinite Vitality
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the cloud-piercing peaks of Zhangjiajie to the tech-driven streets of Shenzhen and the cassava farms of Vietnam. We meet extreme athletes redefining personal limits, turning vertical cliffs and open skies into new playgrounds. Then, we ride in a fully autonomous robotaxi through Shenzhen traffic, exploring the technology and regulations accelerating the global race for self-driving cars. Finally, we travel to Vietnam, where Chinese investment and expertise have transformed the cassava industry—boosting yields, stabilizing farmer incomes, and creating resilient supply chains reaching global markets. From skies to roads to fields, this episode shows how China’s dynamism is reshaping landscapes and lives worldwide.

programme.title: Summer Davos 2026: The Future of Jobs, Skills, and Sustainable Growth
programme.desc: Global trade is undergoing profound change as economies grapple with shifting supply chains, rapid advances in artificial intelligence, and the transition to cleaner energy. We are coming to you from the Summer Davos Forum in Dalian, where policymakers, business leaders, and academics from around the world are discussing how to navigate these transformations. One key question at this year's forum is how these changes will affect workers, and whether they will create new opportunities or deepen existing challenges. To discuss the future of jobs, skills, and sustainable growth, Song Ruixin is joined by Professor Mercedes Maroto-Valer, Deputy Principal for Global Sustainability at Heriot-Watt University, and Kathleen Alexander, co-founder and CEO of Savor, a San Jose based food startup.

programme.title: No Power, No AI
programme.desc: Is energy the ultimate bottleneck for artificial intelligence? As compute demand skyrockets, can our power grids keep up? CGTN's Michael Wang moderates a critical panel at the 2026 Summer Davos Forum on the intersection of AI and energy infrastructure. We'll explore how to align capital investment, infrastructure build-out, and policy frameworks; future-proof energy supply systems to strengthen energy security; and build a more inclusive, sustainable AI-powered energy future. Tune in as global leaders tackle the energy challenge powering the next wave of AI. #SummerDavos2026

programme.title: Observing Europe-So many UK Prime Ministers, same old problems
programme.desc: Since moving to London, CGTN's Li Jianhua has witnessed the UK cycle through four leaders. In this video, Jianhua reflects on the problems facing each of those prime ministers… and why it's affected how he buys grapes.

programme.title: Observing Europe-Who owns Britain?
programme.desc: One of the first things that surprised CGTN's Li Jianhua after moving to Britain was discovering that London’s iconic black cabs are made by a subsidiary of China’s Geely. It’s not alone. Jaguar Land Rover belongs to India’s Tata, Mini is owned by Germany’s BMW, and many of Britain’s airports, utilities and landmark buildings have foreign owners. For decades, Britain embraced global investment. But the battle over British Steel suggests attitudes are changing. As concerns grow around national security and economic resilience, the question is no longer just who invests in Britain — but which industries are too strategic to be foreign-owned. In this latest episode of his series Observing Europe, Jianhua explores ownership, investment – and where Britain is drawing the line.

programme.title: Observing Europe - Is migration "weaponized" in Europe?
programme.desc: Schengen - one of Europe’s greatest achievements - is being tested. The Schengen Area promised border-free travel across much of Europe. But migration, security concerns and increasingly polarized politics are putting that promise under pressure. From Ceuta to the return of internal border checks, CGTN Europe correspondent Li Jianhua looks at how Europe’s migration debate is reshaping Schengen — and asks: Can Europe keep its internal borders open as political pressure to control migration grows?

programme.desc: Since moving to London, CGTN's Li Jianhua has witnessed the UK cycle through four leaders. In this video, Jianhua reflects on the problems facing each of those prime ministers… and why it's affected how he buys grapes.

programme.title: Observing Europe-Who owns Britain?
programme.desc: One of the first things that surprised CGTN's Li Jianhua after moving to Britain was discovering that London’s iconic black cabs are made by a subsidiary of China’s Geely. It’s not alone. Jaguar Land Rover belongs to India’s Tata, Mini is owned by Germany’s BMW, and many of Britain’s airports, utilities and landmark buildings have foreign owners. For decades, Britain embraced global investment. But the battle over British Steel suggests attitudes are changing. As concerns grow around national security and economic resilience, the question is no longer just who invests in Britain — but which industries are too strategic to be foreign-owned. In this latest episode of his series Observing Europe, Jianhua explores ownership, investment – and where Britain is drawing the line.

programme.title: Observing Europe - Is migration "weaponized" in Europe?
programme.desc: Schengen - one of Europe’s greatest achievements - is being tested. The Schengen Area promised border-free travel across much of Europe. But migration, security concerns and increasingly polarized politics are putting that promise under pressure. From Ceuta to the return of internal border checks, CGTN Europe correspondent Li Jianhua looks at how Europe’s migration debate is reshaping Schengen — and asks: Can Europe keep its internal borders open as political pressure to control migration grows?

programme.title: BizTalk | AI-powered travel reshaping global tourism
programme.desc: China’s tourism market has continued to heat up this summer. Behind this boom, artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how people travel and is opening up new opportunities for the industry – from personalized itineraries to immersive experiences. In this episode of BizTalk, guests from the World Economic Forum, the World Travel & Tourism Council and Atout France explore how smart technologies can enhance visitor experiences, optimize destination management and unlock new growth opportunities. They also examine what China's emerging "AI tourism" focus could offer the global tourism industry.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-3 Shaolin Style
programme.desc: Episode 3, Shaolin, explores how this thousand-year-old temple has evolved into a unique “kung fu platform” that draws enthusiasts from around the world. Host Kleber immerses himself in Shaolin’s integrated way of life, where Chan (Zen) practice and martial training go hand in hand, and turns the camera toward foreign practitioners pursuing their kung fu dreams both inside and beyond the temple gates. Along the way, he meets international disciples living and training at Shaolin, as well as students learning the rare art of Shaolin Xinyiba under Master Hu Zhengsheng, a former Shaolin monk. At martial arts schools near Songshan Mountain, Kleber also encounters overseas competitors training hard for the arena. Together, their stories reveal Shaolin kung fu’s enduring pull, one that crosses cultures and borders while uniting practitioners through tradition, discipline, and self-mastery.

programme.title: Foodwise: Xilingol
programme.desc: The Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region is located in the northern part of China, stretching from northeast to southwest side. In Xilin Gol, the horses, sheep and cows could be found every where. The local cuisines here are so attractive to the tourists, such as the roasted lamb is a traditional local dish. And the fired stone fried lamb is so hard to find if you are not traveling to Inner Mongolia. Have you ever tried salted milk tea? Just join in this visual trip！

programme.title: Foodwise: Kunming
programme.desc: Join host Tianran He in Kunming, the capital of Yunnan province in southwest China. Named the Spring City for its perennially good weather, Kunming is one of China's most ethnically diverse cities, something that's reflected in its food: From boozy sticky rice for breakfast, to the famous "Crossing the Bridge" rice noodles, and evening barbecues, there's plenty on offer here. Also, it's mushroom season, and Tianran is taking to the hills to hunt for wild fungi – but he'll need a trusty friend to steer him away from the poisonous ones!

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-3 Shaolin Style
programme.desc: Episode 3, Shaolin, explores how this thousand-year-old temple has evolved into a unique “kung fu platform” that draws enthusiasts from around the world. Host Kleber immerses himself in Shaolin’s integrated way of life, where Chan (Zen) practice and martial training go hand in hand, and turns the camera toward foreign practitioners pursuing their kung fu dreams both inside and beyond the temple gates. Along the way, he meets international disciples living and training at Shaolin, as well as students learning the rare art of Shaolin Xinyiba under Master Hu Zhengsheng, a former Shaolin monk. At martial arts schools near Songshan Mountain, Kleber also encounters overseas competitors training hard for the arena. Together, their stories reveal Shaolin kung fu’s enduring pull, one that crosses cultures and borders while uniting practitioners through tradition, discipline, and self-mastery.

programme.title: China Untapped: Changsha
programme.desc: The city of Changsha is one of central China's powerhouses. It's a leader in both the construction machinery industry and in media – Changsha was China's first UNESCO "Creative City". It's also one of China's best-known cities for its nightlife. The soul of a city is in its people, and this episode focuses on the women of Changsha who are helping to innovate, change and further develop this city they call home.

programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He continues his journey through Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. He meets the Lhoba people, China’s smallest ethnic group, who show him their traditional hunting attire. At a sacred lake, Tianran visits an ancient monastery and witnesses the 3000-year-old dance of the Gongbo Tibetans, before venturing to a remote village to experience their their way of life.

programme.title: Young dancer of Batang melody
programme.desc: Tibetan girl Tashi Badro from Batang, Ganzi, Sichuan has learned how to do the Xianzi dance both from her mom and a school program. Batang Xianzi is a unique folk dance of the Tibetan ethnic group with a history spanning over 1,000 years on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. In order to keep the Tibetan tradition alive, Badro’s school has offered the dance as a cultural activity. Badro said dancing with her classmates is the happiest moment of her day. Watch the graceful movements of Badro and her peers performing the Xianzi dance.

programme.title: Wujiang: The Land of Silk
programme.desc: In this episode, we travel to Wujiang District of Suzhou City on China’s east coast to explore the birthplace of silk. There we discover that silk is not merely a precious fabric but also a way of life. For centuries, Wujiang District has been one of China’s largest‑scale silk‑producing regions, which has turned it into a major commercial hub. Local residents worship a distinctive deity‑the Silkworm Goddess. Per the traditional Chinese lunar calendar, the Lesser Fullness of Grain (Xiaoman) solar term coincides with the goddess’s birthday. Local folk opera troupes take turns staging performances on the stage by the main temple hall over several days to mark the occasion and pray for good fortune. We then learn how silk was manufactured centuries ago, before seeing how imperial‑grade silk is being reinvented for modern‑day fashion.

programme.title: The Tongliang Dragon Dance
programme.desc: The Tongliang Dragon Dance is a traditional performance art rooted in Chongqing’s Tongliang District, characterized by its elaborate dragon props and dynamic choreography. Originating in the Ming Dynasty and flourishing during the Qing, this vibrant folk tradition has regained its brilliance in modern times and earned international acclaim. The dance consists of two main branches: the dragon lantern dance—featuring forms like the Grand Wriggling Dragon, the Fire Dragon, and the Straw Dragon—and the festive lantern dance, which includes acts such as “Carp Leaps Over the Dragon Gate,” “Mudfish Eating Dumplings,” and “Three Dragons.” Steeped in cultural symbolism, the Tongliang Dragon Dance expresses values of unity, vitality, and harmony with nature. While a few iconic forms like the Fire Dragon remain widely recognized, many others are on the verge of extinction and in urgent need of preservation. In this episode, the host travels to Chongqing to meet with four inheritors of the Tongliang Dragon Dance. Through their stories, we uncover the rich legacy of this dazzling tradition, explore the deep roots of dragon culture in the region, and trace the origins of one of China’s most awe-inspiring folk arts.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.2
programme.desc: Tianran He explores Lhasa’s bustling Barkhor Street, where pilgrims, locals, and visitors alike circle its ancient lanes. This multicultural district, home to sacred temples and boutique shops, becomes the backdrop as Tianran dons traditional Tibetan attire for a photoshoot. Across the city, he meets high school students dancing for Douyin — China’s version of TikTok, blending street dance with traditional Tibetan moves. Finally, Tianran travels to the birthplace of Tibetan incense, where waterwheels still power this thousand-year-old craft.

programme.desc: The Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region is located in the northern part of China, stretching from northeast to southwest side. In Xilin Gol, the horses, sheep and cows could be found every where. The local cuisines here are so attractive to the tourists, such as the roasted lamb is a traditional local dish. And the fired stone fried lamb is so hard to find if you are not traveling to Inner Mongolia. Have you ever tried salted milk tea? Just join in this visual trip！

programme.title: Foodwise: Kunming
programme.desc: Join host Tianran He in Kunming, the capital of Yunnan province in southwest China. Named the Spring City for its perennially good weather, Kunming is one of China's most ethnically diverse cities, something that's reflected in its food: From boozy sticky rice for breakfast, to the famous "Crossing the Bridge" rice noodles, and evening barbecues, there's plenty on offer here. Also, it's mushroom season, and Tianran is taking to the hills to hunt for wild fungi – but he'll need a trusty friend to steer him away from the poisonous ones!

programme.title: Foodwise: The Taste of Home
programme.desc: In this episode, our hosts Tianran He and Eva May eat their way down memory lane across virtual space and different time zones, and embark on a culinary journey at their birthplace. Eva rediscovers her love for a classic century-old dish in her hometown Vienna and introduces Austria's long-lasting coffeehouse culture to Tianran, who also joins her virtually for an evening with friends and food the traditional Viennese way. Meanwhile, Beijing's charming autumn season sets Tianran back in time as he rediscovers flavors from his childhood. His passion for tea might have even started in one of the old tea shops in Beijing's hutongs, recollecting his memories one sip at a time, accompanied by nostalgic meals and a relaxed stroll under yellow gingko trees.

programme.title: Foodwise: Shaoxing
programme.desc: Join host Tianran He in the historic water town of Shaoxing, famed for its yellow wine. Traversing its canals by boat, Tianran discovers why it's said there are 10,000 bridges in Shaoxing, before enjoying the freshest catch of the day. But as it turns out, Shaoxing's climate is also perfect for fermentation, leading to a wide array of unique local foods that can sometimes be both smelly and delicious – and at other times, downright unforgettable!

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-4 Medieval Combat
programme.desc: Episode 4 centres on Shanghai, where Eastern and Western martial traditions meet in surprising ways. Kleber visits local practitioners of Historical European Martial Arts (HEMA), trying German and Italian longsword techniques first-hand and seeing how Chinese enthusiasts innovate by combining European swordsmanship with ancient Chinese military manuals. The episode also follows the rise of BUHURT, a European-style armored combat sport now gaining traction in China, featuring locally made traditional Chinese armour in intense full-contact bouts. Through Kleber’s own multicultural martial arts studio and the city’s everyday East-West blend, the episode shows Shanghai as a global hub, a place where classical martial arts find new life and cross-cultural practices thrive.

programme.title: China Untapped: Huzhou
programme.desc: Located in the east of China, on the south shore of Taihu Lake, Huzhou has been well-known for its richness in resources and blooming in silk trade since the ancient times. Guided by the concept of "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets", Huzhou now is committed to developing green industries. In this episode, CGTN hosts Tianran He and Hannah Wilson travelled to Huzhou, where they tried a variety of guesthouse hotels in the Moganshan Mountains; experienced the life of digital nomads in Anji’s countryside; learned about the eco-concepts behind China's traditional architectures in Nanxun Ancient Town; and explored the development of eco-agriculture powered by high-tech along the Taihu Lake. All these phenomena demonstrate that economic development and environmental protection can achieve harmonious coexistence, and that civilization thrives if ecology is prosperous.

programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.3
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He rounds off his travels through Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. He journeys into the Yarlung Zangbo Grand Canyon – one of the largest and deepest canyons on Earth, and along the way, tries to catch a glimpse of Mount Namcha Barwa, the easternmost peak of the Himalayas. Instead, he encounters a waterfall said to be a gateway to the afterlife, before finally arriving at the entrance to the canyon.

programme.title: Face-changing wonder boy
programme.desc: Face-changing is an ancient Chinese performance art that is a component of Sichuan opera. Hu Yibo, 13, learned the act from his grandfather and other experienced masters. Dressed in brightly-colored costumes and while changing from one mask to another in just the blink of an eye, Yibo skillfully swipes open a fan to hide his "magical" movements. As a young inheritor, he undertakes daily training to perfect his skill set in the hope of becoming a master one day.

programme.title: Qingdao: The Jade Island
programme.desc: To boost Qingdao’s international‑oriented publicity and build its profile as an international tourist city, this episode takes us to Qingdao. Through three segments‑‑Modern Qingdao, Historic Qingdao and Internationalized Qingdao, we showcase the diverse facets of this charming city.

programme.title: Living Arts of Huizhou
programme.desc: This is Huangshan in eastern China. In this city, you’ll encounter one of China’s most traditional building styles: Hui-style architecture. How does Hui style set this region apart? What’s life like for people living in these houses? With these questions in mind, we’re embarking on a journey to decode Hui-style architecture.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.3
programme.desc: Join Tianran He on a high-speed train to Shigatse, gateway to the Himalayas and home to Mount Qomolangma, the world’s highest peak. As the city with the most land ports in Xizang, Shigatse serves as a key corridor to South Asia. Here, Tianran samples breakfast at a bustling local teahouse and experiences monastic life at the vast Tashilunpo Monastery. He then visits an agricultural park where tropical crops thrive against the odds of the alpine plateau, before discovering pulu — a traditional Tibetan textile now earning global acclaim.

programme.title: Shenzhen：When Travel meets Technology
programme.desc: In the second episode of the Shenzhen series, we adopt high-tech aerial shooting and follow the host on a city tour, letting audiences experience Shenzhen’s vigorous development, lush ecological scenery and cutting-edge technological strength.
